|lore=“I’m not afraid.” “Oh. You will be. You will be.” One of the lessons Luke learned was that fear of the unknown can be stronger than fear of the known.
|game_text=Lose the top card of your Reserve Deck to make a just drawn destiny lost. OR When this card is drawn for destiny, you may place an Effect that is not [Immune to Alter] into owner's Used Pile.
|printings={{Card versions/Fear (Dagobah)}}
|notes=The Players Committee released the original-layout slip for Fear on 30 May 2003. The published Set 5 editions are linked as [[Fear (V) (Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time)|Original]] and [[Fear (V) (Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time) (Errata)|Remastered (2006)]]. The first sheet was released 30 May 2003 and became tournament legal on 6 June. The remastered wording specifies that the Effect being moved to its owner’s Used Pile is on table. The original refers to an Effect in the same drawn-destiny action, subject to the [https://web.archive.org/web/20090816063441id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/AR/AR1.7.1.pdf#page=22 period rule on active cards]. The [https://web.archive.org/web/20090816063441id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/AR/AR1.7.1.pdf#page=29 period example] distinguishes drawing Fear for destiny from using its value while it is stacked. This is the Set 5 Interrupt based on [[Fear]].
|sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20030801181811/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/vcards/SWCCGVirtualSet5.pdf Virtual Set #5 first release sheet] (theforce.net, 30 May 2003; Internet Archive 1 August 2003), page 3, slip 36.
* [https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards5.pdf Virtual Set #5 revised sheet] (publisher index dates the edition 19 June 2003), res.starwarsccg.org, page 3, slip 36.
